phrases.tip: Olá works throughout the day.

phrases.situation: You greet someone in the morning.
phrases.tip: Use bom dia in the morning; boa tarde in the afternoon.

phrases.situation: You ask a friend their name.
phrases.tip: Te is informal. Como se chama? is a polite alternative.
O meu nome means my name. Replace Ana with your own name.

phrases.situation: You say where you are from.
phrases.tip: Sou is the eu form of ser. De Portugal has no article.
This short phrase is a natural response to an introduction.
Pode + infinitive makes a polite request.

phrases.situation: You will see your friend tomorrow.
phrases.tip: Até means until; amanhã means tomorrow.

title: At the café
goal: Order, count and ask for the bill

phrases.en: I would like a coffee, please.
phrases.tip: Queria is a polite way to order. Um café is one coffee.

phrases.en: I would like two coffees, please.
phrases.tip: Dois is masculine. Notice the plural cafés.

phrases.en: I would like a bread roll, please.
phrases.tip: Um pão becomes dois pães in the plural.

phrases.pt: Queria um café e um leite, por favor.
phrases.en: I would like a coffee and a milk, please.
phrases.tip: E joins the items. Um accompanies each masculine noun.

phrases.pt: Queria duas sopas e um pão, por favor.
phrases.en: I would like two soups and a bread roll, please.
phrases.situation: You order a small lunch for two.
phrases.tip: Duas agrees with the feminine noun sopas.

phrases.pt: Queria três águas e dois cafés, por favor.
phrases.en: I would like three waters and two coffees, please.
phrases.situation: You order drinks for a group.
phrases.tip: Três does not change with gender. Águas and cafés are plural.
A conta is a feminine noun; keep the article with the word.
A male speaker normally says obrigado; a female speaker says obrigada.

title: At the market
goal: Ask prices and buy everyday things

phrases.situation: You point to one item and ask its price.
phrases.tip: For several items, ask Quanto custam?

phrases.en: I would like two apples, please.
phrases.situation: You buy apples at a market.
phrases.tip: Maçã is feminine; duas agrees with maçãs.

phrases.en: I would like a kilo of oranges.
phrases.situation: You ask the vendor for oranges.
phrases.tip: Um quilo de describes a quantity. Laranjas is plural.

phrases.situation: You ask a shopkeeper whether bread is available.
phrases.tip: Tem is a polite third-person form of ter.
Caro describes a masculine item; cara describes a feminine one.
Posso + infinitive means can I. Com cartão means by card.

phrases.en: I would like a bag, please.
phrases.situation: You need a bag for your shopping.
phrases.tip: Use por favor to make a request politely.

phrases.en: I do not need a bag.
phrases.situation: You brought your own shopping bag.
phrases.tip: Precisar de means to need. Não makes the sentence negative.

title: Around town
goal: Find your way and use transport

phrases.tip: Onde fica asks where a place is located.
À is the contraction of a + a. À esquerda means on the left.

phrases.situation: You point someone in the right direction.
phrases.tip: Compare à esquerda with à direita.
Siga is a polite instruction. Em frente means straight ahead.

phrases.en: I would like a ticket to Lisbon.
phrases.tip: Para introduces the destination.

phrases.pt: Este autocarro vai para o centro?
phrases.en: Does this bus go to the city centre?
phrases.tip: Autocarro is the European Portuguese word for bus.

phrases.situation: You need help finding your way.
phrases.tip: A female speaker says Estou perdida. Estar describes the current state.

title: At home
goal: Talk about your home and daily life

phrases.situation: You tell someone where you live.
phrases.tip: Morar em describes where you live.
Minha and pequena agree with the feminine noun casa.

phrases.en: The book is on the table.
phrases.situation: You explain where an object is.
phrases.tip: Na is em + a. Estar gives the location of an object.
Tenho is the eu form of ter.

phrases.situation: You say what you plan to do.
phrases.tip: Vou + infinitive expresses a future plan.

phrases.situation: You say what you are doing now.
phrases.tip: In Portugal, estar a + infinitive commonly describes an action in progress.

phrases.situation: You ask someone you know to open a window.
phrases.tip: Podes is informal. Pode is a polite alternative.

phrases.situation: You are looking for your keys.
phrases.tip: Estão is plural because chaves is plural.

title: Feeling better
goal: Explain how you feel and ask for help

phrases.situation: You tell someone you feel unwell.
phrases.tip: Sinto-me bem means I feel well; não makes it negative.
Use ter for febre: Tenho febre.
Precisar de + a noun expresses a need.

phrases.en: I would like to book an appointment.
phrases.tip: Marcar uma consulta means to book an appointment.

phrases.situation: Someone asks how you feel today.
phrases.tip: Melhor compares your current state with before.
A female speaker says Estou cansada. Estar describes a temporary state.
